name: remote-desktop
description: A Linux desktop streamed into a tab as low-latency H.264 video with full keyboard, mouse, clipboard and cursor control; the desktop follows the tab's size. Powered by QuicDesk, whose server ships in this package for Linux x86_64 and arm64.

remoteDesktop.mode.description: Managed: start a virtual display (Xvfb) and a desktop session on it, and let the desktop follow the tab's size. Existing: attach to a display that is already running, such as :0 on a desktop machine; input goes to that real screen and its size is never changed. Takes effect on the next Start.

remoteDesktop.display.description: The X display to create (managed mode) or to attach to (existing mode), e.g. ":101" or ":0".

remoteDesktop.desktopCommand.description: Managed mode only: the command that starts the desktop environment (e.g. xfce4-session, startlxde, mate-session). Must be installed on the host.

remoteDesktop.keyboardLayout.description: Managed mode only: XKB layout applied to the virtual display (setxkbmap), e.g. us, de, fr. Keys are forwarded by physical position, so this should match the keyboard you type on.

remoteDesktop.port.description: Preferred loopback port for the stream. If it is taken, the next free port is used.

remoteDesktop.fps.description: Capture rate cap in frames per second. A static screen costs almost nothing regardless. Takes effect on the next Start.

remoteDesktop.bitrateKbps.description: Video bitrate cap in kilobits per second. The stream adapts below it when the connection struggles. Takes effect on the next Start.

remoteDesktop.pixelRatio.description: Default remote pixels per CSS pixel for your devices. Auto detects each device's pixel ratio (capped at 2, so a 3x phone gets a 2x desktop). Each browser can override this for itself from the viewer tab's pixel-ratio button; the desktop follows the ratio of the tab that drives it.

remoteDesktop.dpi.description: Managed mode only: DPI reported to apps on the virtual display.

remoteDesktop.serverPath.description: Path to your own quicdesk-server build. Leave empty to use the one shipped with this extension (Linux x86_64 and arm64), then PATH, then ~/.cargo/bin.
